note: Bundled evidence corpus used ONLY in simulated mode (no TAVILY_API_KEY). Documents are real public facts with their publication dates so the temporal engine has something honest to reason about. In live mode Tavily replaces this corpus entirely.

documents.title: What's New In Python 3.13
documents.content: Python 3.13 was released on October 7, 2024. It introduces an experimental free-threaded build, an improved interactive interpreter, and changes to the deprecated modules. Python 3.13 is the current stable feature release; the documentation recommends 3.13 for new projects requiring the newest language features.

documents.title: What's New In Python 3.12
documents.content: Python 3.12 was released on October 2, 2023. It added improved error messages, PEP 701 f-string grammar, and per-interpreter GIL groundwork. Python 3.12 is in security-fix status once 3.13 shipped.

documents.title: PEP 373 – Python 2.7 Release Schedule
documents.content: Python 2.7 reached end of life on January 1, 2020. No further bug fixes, security patches, or releases are planned for Python 2.7. Projects still running Python 2.7 are unsupported.

documents.title: React v19
documents.content: React 19 was released as stable on December 5, 2024. It includes Actions, the use() hook, server components support in the stable channel, and improved hydration error reporting. React 19 supersedes React 18 as the current major release.

documents.title: React v18.0
documents.content: React 18 was released on March 29, 2022, introducing concurrent rendering and automatic batching. React 18 is no longer the latest major version following the release of React 19 in December 2024.

documents.title: Node.js Releases
documents.content: Node.js 18 reached end of life on April 30, 2025 and no longer receives security updates. Node.js 20 is in maintenance and Node.js 22 is the active LTS line as of the 2025 release schedule.

documents.title: RFC 9114: HTTP/3
documents.content: HTTP/3 is defined in RFC 9114, published in June 2022. HTTP/3 runs over QUIC rather than TCP and is the third major version of the HTTP protocol.

documents.title: RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3
documents.content: TLS 1.3 is specified in RFC 8446, published in August 2018. It removes static RSA and CBC ciphersuites and reduces the handshake to one round trip.

documents.title: PostgreSQL 17 Released
documents.content: PostgreSQL 17 was released on September 26, 2024. It improves vacuum memory management, adds incremental backup support, and improves the JSON_TABLE implementation. PostgreSQL 17 supersedes 16 as the current major release.

documents.title: PostgreSQL 16 Released
documents.content: PostgreSQL 16 was released on September 14, 2023, with parallel query improvements and logical replication from standbys. It is no longer the newest major version after the September 2024 release of PostgreSQL 17.

documents.title: Tailwind CSS v4.0
documents.content: Tailwind CSS v4.0 was released on January 22, 2025. It moves configuration into CSS with the @theme directive and ships a new Oxide engine that produces faster builds. v4 supersedes v3 as the current major version.

documents.title: Announcing Vite 6
documents.content: Vite 6 was released on November 26, 2024, introducing the Environment API and a new default resolver. Vite 6 replaced Vite 5 as the current major version.

documents.title: WHO statement on the fifteenth IHR Emergency Committee meeting regarding COVID-19
documents.content: The WHO Director-General determined on May 5, 2023 that COVID-19 no longer constitutes a public health emergency of international concern. The emergency committee's advice was accepted and the PHEIC status ended on that date.

documents.title: Mount Everest remeasured: 8,848.86 m
documents.content: China and Nepal jointly announced on December 8, 2020 that the height of Mount Everest is 8,848.86 metres. The figure supersedes the earlier 8,848 m (Nepal) and 8,844.43 m (China) values.

documents.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — Artificial Intelligence Act
documents.content: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act entered into force on August 1, 2024. Prohibitions applied from February 2, 2025 and obligations for general-purpose AI model providers applied from August 2, 2025. The regulation is being phased in through 2027.

documents.title: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
documents.content: The GDPR (Regulation 2016/679) was adopted on April 27, 2016 and became applicable on May 25, 2018. It remains in force and applies to any organisation processing personal data of people in the EU.

documents.title: GPT-4
documents.content: OpenAI announced GPT-4 on March 14, 2023. GPT-4 is a large multimodal model that accepts image and text inputs and produces text outputs, with a context window of 32,768 tokens in the initial release.

documents.title: Gemini 1.5: our next-generation model
documents.content: Google announced Gemini 1.5 Pro on February 15, 2024 with a 1 million token context window in limited preview. The model uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture for efficiency.

documents.title: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS released
documents.content: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS 'Noble Numbat' was released on April 25, 2024 with standard support until April 2029. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS remains supported, with standard support ending in April 2027.

documents.title: The International System of Units (SI Brochure), 9th edition
documents.content: The metre is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum, c, to be 299 792 458 when expressed in the unit m/s. This definition has been in force since 1983 and was retained in the 2019 SI redefinition.

documents.title: Node.js Release Working Group schedule
documents.content: Node.js 18 'Hydrogen' entered Active LTS in October 2022. The release schedule at the time listed Node.js 18 as the newest LTS line and Node.js 19 as the current release line.

documents.title: Why you should upgrade to Python 3.7
documents.content: Python 3.7 is the newest version of Python available today and should be used for all new projects. Python 3.7 introduced dataclasses and brings the language to its modern form.

documents.title: Django 5.1 release notes
documents.content: Django 5.1 was released on August 7, 2024 and is the newest stable release of Django, superseding Django 5.0. Django 4.2 is an LTS release that continues to receive security fixes until April 2026; it is no longer the newest stable release but it is still supported. Django 5.1 requires Python 3.10 or later.

documents.title: Kubernetes v1.32 released
documents.content: Kubernetes 1.32 was released on December 11, 2024 and is the newest stable release of Kubernetes, superseding Kubernetes 1.31. Kubernetes 1.28 reached end of life in October 2024 and no longer receives patch releases. Each Kubernetes minor release is supported for approximately 14 months.

documents.title: Oracle Java SE support roadmap
documents.content: Java 21 is the newest long-term support release of Java and supersedes Java 17 as the current LTS baseline. Java 17 remains a long-term support release that receives updates until September 2029. Java 25 is scheduled as the next long-term support release.
